visualCard.title: Carboxylic Acid Derivative Reactivity Ski-Slope, Resonance Stabilization & IR Frequencies

items.label: Typical acyl-derivative reactivity ladder
items.text: Acid Chloride (RCOCl) > Acid Anhydride > Thioester (RCOSR′) > Ester (RCOOR′) > Amide (RCONR′₂) > Carboxylate Ion (RCOO⁻).

items.label: Two Governing Factors: Leaving Group Basicity + Ground-State Resonance
items.text: Cl⁻ (pKaH −7) is the weakest base and 3p Cl has poor π overlap with 2p C; –NR₂ (pKaH ~38) is a terrible leaving group and 2p N donates strongly into C=O!

items.label: IR Carbonyl Stretch Mirrors Double-Bond Character
items.text: Stronger resonance donation into C=O weakens the C=O bond (more single-bond character → lower wavenumber): Acid Chloride (1800 cm⁻¹) > Ester (1735 cm⁻¹) > Ketone (1715 cm⁻¹) > Amide (1650 cm⁻¹).

chips: Reactivity: Acid Chloride > Anhydride > Thioester > Ester > Amide > RCOO⁻

High reactivity; TWO IR C=O peaks (~1810 & 1760 cm⁻¹)
Least reactive neutral derivative; IR C=O ~1650 cm⁻¹

payload.title: Recognize acid derivatives
payload.fullNote: Acyl C → O–C: ester. Acyl C → N: amide. Acyl C → O → acyl C: anhydride. For esters, name the O-alkyl group then the acid-derived -oate. Amides use -amide, with N- prefixes for N substituents. Anhydrides use the acid name(s) plus anhydride; list both acids for a mixed anhydride. In lactam/lactone shorthand, beta = four ring atoms, gamma = five, delta = six; count the ring heteroatom and carbonyl carbon, excluding the exocyclic oxygen.

visualCard.title: Why Are Thioesters (Acetyl-CoA) So Much More Reactive Than Oxygen Esters?
visualCard.prompt: Compare Thioesters (R–CO–SR′), Oxygen Esters (R–CO–OR′), and Amides (R–CO–NR′₂):

items.label: Thioester vs. Oxygen Ester Orbital Overlap
items.outcome: 3p Sulfur Has Poor π Overlap with 2p Carbon!
items.text: Because the C–S bond is long and 3p/2p orbitals mismatch in size, sulfur gives very little resonance stabilization to C=O (leaving the carbonyl carbon highly δ+).

items.label: Thiolate (RS⁻) vs. Alkoxide (RO⁻) Leaving Group
items.outcome: RS⁻ (pKaH ~10) Is a Much Better Leaving Group Than RO⁻ (pKaH ~16)
items.text: Thioesters sit right below anhydrides in reactivity—stable enough to survive in water, yet reactive enough for enzymatic acyl transfer!

items.label: Why Does an Anhydride Show TWO C=O IR Peaks?
items.outcome: Symmetric (~1810 cm⁻¹) and Asymmetric (~1760 cm⁻¹) Coupled Stretches
items.text: Two C=O bonds joined through a central oxygen vibrate in-phase and out-of-phase, giving a diagnostic doublet in IR!

payload.fullNote: An ether has no adjacent carbonyl. An N-substituted amide is still an amide even if it has no N–H bond. Ring size names count heteroatoms as ring members. steps.label: 1. Add to the carbonyl
steps.text: Hydroxide attacks the ester carbonyl carbon while the pi pair moves to oxygen. The arrow shows that pi-pair movement, not the entire mechanism.

steps.label: 2. Tetrahedral intermediate
steps.text: The carbon now bears the incoming OH, the original OCH3, and an O− derived from the carbonyl oxygen. It has four single bonds. Four directions are spread in a 2D projection for readability, not a claim of 90-degree physical bond angles.

payload.title: Acyl substitution and relative reactivity
payload.fullNote: A nucleophile adds to an acyl carbon and shifts the pi pair to O. Collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate reforms C=O and expels a leaving group. For comparable unactivated derivatives, a useful order is acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide. Leaving-group basicity and resonance donation both matter. Inductive withdrawal transmits through sigma bonds and can increase acyl-carbon electrophilicity. Steric crowding can hinder nucleophile approach. These effects compete with leaving-group ability, resonance and catalysis; a single naming-priority or conjugation shortcut cannot rank every reaction.

visualCard.title: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Mechanism & Organometallic / Hydride Selectivity

items.label: Two-Step Addition–Elimination Pathway
items.text: Step 1: Nucleophile attacks sp² C=O to form a tetrahedral sp³ intermediate. Step 2: Carbonyl π bond reforms and kicks out the WEAKEST base (best leaving group).

items.label: Grignard / Organolithium + Ester or Acid Chloride (2 Equivalents!)
items.text: First equivalent forms a ketone in situ; because a ketone is MORE reactive than an ester, a second RMgBr immediately attacks to yield a tertiary alcohol (R′–C(OH)R₂).

items.label: Stopping at the Ketone or Aldehyde
items.text: Acid Chloride + R₂CuLi (Gilman) stops at the KETONE; Ester + DIBAL-H at −78 °C (or Acid Chloride + LiAl(Ot-Bu)₃H) stops at the ALDEHYDE.

payload.title: Acyl substitution and relative reactivity
payload.fullNote: Aldehydes and ketones normally add rather than substitute because hydride or an ordinary carbanion would be a poor leaving group. Conjugation means adjacent aligned p orbitals delocalize electrons; it can stabilize a reactant, intermediate or transition state. A rate depends on the activation free-energy difference, so stabilization alone does not prove a faster reaction. Enones also offer beta attack (1,4-addition), which differs from direct carbonyl attack (1,2-addition). Heteroatom lone-pair donation into C=O, especially from amide N, reduces carbonyl electrophilicity. The effect of conjugation requires the actual substrate, nucleophile, site and conditions.

visualCard.title: Stopping Ester + Grignard at the Ketone or Cleaving the C–N Bond in Amide + LiAlH₄

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Reacting ethyl benzoate with 1 eq CH₃MgBr to get acetophenone cleanly, or reducing an amide with LiAlH₄ to get an alcohol + amine.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Ketones are more reactive than esters, so Ester + RMgBr always double-adds to a 3° alcohol; Amide + LiAlH₄ keeps the C–N bond intact and reduces C=O to CH₂ (forming an amine)!

payload.fullNote: Amide resonance makes peptide bonds relatively resistant to uncatalyzed hydrolysis. Strained beta-lactams are more reactive than ordinary unstrained amides. Small rings can have angle strain and torsional strain. Beta-lactam geometry can reduce optimal amide orbital overlap and hydrolysis can relieve strain; the extent of nitrogen pyramidalization and resonance loss depends on ring fusion/substitution. The displayed unfused four-membered connectivity diagram is not a 3D bond-angle model.

visualCard.title: Chymotrypsin Acyl-Enzyme Mechanism (Catalytic Triad: Ser-195, His-57, Asp-102)

items.label: Phase 1: Acylation (Peptide C–N Cleaved)
items.outcome: Ser-195 –OH (Deprotonated by His-57) Attacks Amide C=O
items.text: Forms Tetrahedral Intermediate #1 (stabilized by the oxyanion hole), which collapses to release the C-terminal amine fragment and form a covalent Ester (Acyl-Enzyme).

items.label: Phase 2: Deacylation (Enzyme Regenerated)
items.outcome: Water (Activated by His-57) Hydrolyzes the Serine Ester
items.text: Forms Tetrahedral Intermediate #2, expelling Ser-195 –OH and releasing the N-terminal carboxylic acid fragment.

items.label: Why Asp-102 Is Essential
items.outcome: Electrostatic Anchor + Tautomer Lock on His-57
items.text: Asp-102’s carboxylate (−1) stabilizes the imidazolium (+1) ion formed when His-57 accepts the proton from Ser-195.

payload.title: Hydrolysis, alcoholysis, and transesterification
payload.fullNote: Anhydrides react with water to give acids, with alcohols to give ester plus acid, and with amines to give amide plus acid-derived products. Transesterification exchanges one OR group for another under suitable catalysis. Acidic amide hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid and protonated amine; basic hydrolysis gives carboxylate and amine. A condensation joins reactants while losing a small molecule. Fischer esterification is acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water under acid catalysis; removing water or using excess alcohol favors ester. Water need not be completely absent, and aqueous acid promotes the reverse hydrolysis.

visualCard.title: Hydrolysis, Alcoholysis, Transesterification, Aminolysis & Cyclic Derivatives (Lactones/Lactams)

items.label: Universal Hydrolysis Endpoint
items.text: Every carboxylic acid derivative (acid chloride, anhydride, ester, amide, nitrile) hydrolyzes in hot aqueous acid (H₃O⁺, Δ) to a carboxylic acid (RCOOH) or in base (HO⁻, Δ) to a carboxylate (RCOO⁻).

items.label: Transesterification & Matched Alkoxide Rule
items.text: RCOOR′ + R″OH (cat. H⁺ or R″O⁻) ⇌ RCOOR″ + R′OH. Whenever using a basic alkoxide catalyst or solvent with an ester, match the alkoxide (R′O⁻/R′OH) unless you WANT transesterification!

items.label: Why Aminolysis of Acid Chlorides Needs 2 Equivalents of Amine
items.text: RCOCl + 2 R′NH₂ → RCONHR′ + R′NH₃⁺Cl⁻. One equivalent forms the amide; a second equivalent of amine (or added pyridine/Et₃N/NaOH) neutralizes the HCl generated!

chips: Lactone = Cyclic Ester | Lactam = Cyclic Amide

Use matched base R″O⁻ with R″OH solvent to prevent scrambling!

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Using NaOCH₂CH₃ in ethanol as the base for a Claisen reaction on a METHYL ester (getting a scrambled methyl/ethyl ester mixture), or splitting a lactone into two separate fragments upon hydrolysis.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Always match the base/solvent to the ester (NaOMe/MeOH for methyl esters); hydrolyzing a cyclic ester (lactone) or cyclic amide (lactam) opens the ring into ONE linear molecule containing both groups!

payload.title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives
objectives: Identify esters, amides, anhydrides, lactones, and lactams

lessonInventory.title: Recognize acid derivatives
lessonInventory.tag: Read the atom directly attached to acyl carbon
lessonInventory.coreRule: Esters have C(=O)–OR; amides have C(=O)–NR2; anhydrides have C(=O)–O–C(=O). Lactones are cyclic esters and lactams are cyclic amides. A beta-lactam contains a four-membered ring.

lessonInventory.title: Acyl substitution and relative reactivity
lessonInventory.coreRule: A nucleophile adds to an acyl carbon and shifts the pi pair to O. Collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate reforms C=O and expels a leaving group. For comparable unactivated derivatives, a useful order is acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide. Leaving-group basicity and resonance donation both matter. Inductive withdrawal transmits through sigma bonds and can increase acyl-carbon electrophilicity. Steric crowding can hinder nucleophile approach. These effects compete with leaving-group ability, resonance and catalysis; a single naming-priority or conjugation shortcut cannot rank every reaction.

lessonInventory.title: Hydrolysis, alcoholysis, and transesterification
lessonInventory.coreRule: Anhydrides react with water to give acids, with alcohols to give ester plus acid, and with amines to give amide plus acid-derived products. Transesterification exchanges one OR group for another under suitable catalysis. Acidic amide hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid and protonated amine; basic hydrolysis gives carboxylate and amine. A condensation joins reactants while losing a small molecule. Fischer esterification is acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water under acid catalysis; removing water or using excess alcohol favors ester. Water need not be completely absent, and aqueous acid promotes the reverse hydrolysis.
